editorial.headline: Rice Retail Is Nationally Open—but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This specialised rice-retail activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration there today.
editorial.body:
Retail rice is a more precise activity than its plain title suggests. It covers the specialised retail sale of a range of rice varieties, including Cianjur, Cisadane, Saigon and glutinous rice. The focus is not merely rice as a commodity, but its sale through a retail activity dedicated to the category and its distinct varieties. That specificity gives the activity a clear commercial identity: a business built around retailing rice in its many recognised forms.

The activity is open across every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. Nationally, its PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. That position is grounded in the cited Presidential Regulations, which are the stated source for its PMA treatment. For a founder reading the national position alone, the signal is straightforward: this is an open activity, available from the smallest listed scale through to Large.

Bali changes that answer decisively. A foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today. The record identifies the Bali status as blocked by risk class: at the Large scale, the OSS risk classification is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. That places the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The result is a registration block in Bali, even though the national position remains fully open to foreign ownership.

The distinction is worth holding clearly. The national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and the activity is open at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. Yet those national facts do not override the Bali moratorium. For this rice-retail activity, national openness describes the ownership position; Bali’s risk-based rule determines whether a PMA registration can proceed on the island. The honest reading is therefore two-part: fully foreign-open nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the permanent moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: This activity is fully foreign-open nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the permanent moratorium.
